title: Rafanata Lucana
author: Marco Bellini
desc: A rustic Basilicata frittata built on grated fresh horseradish root and potato, its sharp, pungent bite a distinctive feature of this simple, satisfying peasant dish.
longDesc: Rafanata takes its name directly from rafano (horseradish), whose sharp bite is mellowed somewhat by cooking but still gives this humble egg dish a distinctive character unlike an ordinary frittata found elsewhere in Italy.
ingredients: 60 g (⅓ cup) fresh horseradish root, peeled and finely grated
60 ml (¼ cup) extra virgin olive oil
steps: Combine the grated boiled potato with the grated horseradish.
Beat the eggs with the pecorino, salt, and pepper.
Stir the potato and horseradish mixture into the beaten eggs.
Warm the olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Pour in the egg mixture, spreading evenly, and cook for 6–8 minutes until the bottom is set and golden.
Carefully flip using a plate, then slide back into the pan to cook the other side for another 5–6 minutes.
Slide onto a board, let rest briefly, then slice into wedges and serve warm.
chefTips: Fresh horseradish root, grated just before use, gives the most pungent, authentic flavor — jarred, prepared horseradish is a milder substitute if needed.
A good non-stick pan makes the flipping process much easier.
This dish is traditionally enjoyed warm rather than piping hot, letting the horseradish flavor come through clearly.
commonMistakes: Using too little horseradish, missing the dish's defining sharp character.
Flipping before the bottom has properly set, resulting in a messy transfer.
Cooking over heat that's too high, browning the outside before the center sets.
storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days; excellent eaten cold or at room temperature.
reheating: Reheat gently in a dry skillet, or enjoy at room temperature.
healthBenefits: A good source of protein and calcium from the eggs and cheese.
culturalNote: Rafanata is a humble, distinctive dish of Basilicata, its pungent fresh horseradish setting it apart from ordinary frittate found elsewhere in Italy.
